pqc_support: Partial — press release only: ML-DSA and SLH-DSA-signed PDFs were exchanged between BFO and Adobe; addition to the PDF specification is underway.
pqc_capability_description: A PDF signed with ML-DSA was exchanged between BFO and Adobe in May 2025; SLH-DSA-signed documents were exchanged soon after. Addition of both algorithms to the PDF specification is being formalized.
pqc_roadmap_details: Addition of ML-DSA and SLH-DSA to the PDF specification is being formalized; the specification is to be finalised and published.
testing_&_validation_methods: Successful exchanges of ML-DSA- and SLH-DSA-signed PDF documents between vendors.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: PQC signatures may be larger and could affect performance in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: PQC integration requires changes across HSM manufacturers, CAs, PDF viewers, and validation tools; RSA- and ECC-signed PDFs remain valid.
organizational_readiness: Vendors, developers, and users must collaborate to implement and adopt the new standards.

evidence.PQC Support: the first PDF signed with the ML-DSA algorithm was exchanged between BFO and Adobe in May 2025, with documents signed with the SLH-DSA algorithm exchanged soon after.
evidence.PQC Capability Description: These successful exchanges between vendors led to an agreement made at PDF Days 2025
evidence.Crypto Primitives: Today's PDF digital signatures rely on robust cryptographic algorithms based on RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC)
evidence.Signature Schemes: including two digital signature algorithms: ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-based Digital Signature Algorithm) and SLH-DSA (Stateless Hash-based Digital Signature Algorithm)
evidence.PQC Roadmap Details: to formalize the addition of these two new post-quantum signature algorithms to the PDF specification.
